newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk presidential palace says no PM warning letter.
newsitem.headline: Turk presidential palace says no PM warning letter.

text.p: Turkey's presidential palace denied on Thursday that President Suleyman Demirel had sent Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan a letter expressing concern the government was at odds with the secular system.
Several newspapers published excerpts from the alleged letter on Thursday, but a presidential palace press officer said: "There is no such letter".
Erbakan described the press reports as "a lie".
"There is a widespread feeling that you are diverting from the secularist, democratic republican aims. This is also my belief," the mass-selling Hurriyet daily quoted Demirel as saying in the letter.

The newspapers said the alleged letter was also copied to armed forces leader Ismail Hakki Karadayi on the eve of a crucial meeting later this week between top politicians and the restive chiefs of the secularist armed forces.
"No, it is all a lie," Erbakan told reporters ahead of a cabinet meeting in Ankara.
Demirel and Erbakan were to hold a regular meeting on Thursday, scheduled for 5.00 p.m. (1500 GMT).

The armed forces have warned Erbakan's Islamist-right coalition in recent weeks against increasing the role of Islam in public life, and these issues are expected to be discussed at Friday's meeting of the National Security Council.
Demirel, himself dislodged as premier during two of the three previous coups, allegedly warned Erbakan against the consequences of upsetting the army and other groups.
